Consult Summary:
32-year-old man with 6 weeks of generalized tiredness and body aches following travel to the USA; had a transient calf rash in late February. Plan is for blood work including Lyme serology and routine panels, with telephone follow-up.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Fatigue and generalized myalgias
- Onset: ~6 weeks ago (mid/late February, ~2 weeks after return from US holiday).
- Course: Persistent; impacting work effectiveness and exercise tolerance; daytime tiredness.
- Associated: Decreased appetite; no weight change. No fever now, no respiratory, GI, GU, or neurologic red-flag symptoms; occasional nonspecific headache.
- Pertinent negatives: No cough, SOB, sore throat currently, chest pain, abdominal pain, bowel or urinary changes, joint swelling.
- Plan: Blood tests (CBC, renal, liver, thyroid, inflammatory markers per doctor statement “all the normal things”) to look for systemic causes.

Issue 2: Transient rash – ?Erythema migrans, query Lyme disease
- Description: Annular/patch rash on posterior calf noticed by wife; minimal itch; appeared mid-to-late February; faded over “a couple of weeks.”
- Possible exposure: Frequent walking in shorts and boots during US trip; no recalled tick bite.
- Associated: Sore throat and possible mild fever at that time.
- Differential: Lyme disease, other post-infective rash.
- Plan: Lyme disease serology included in blood work; treat with appropriate antibiotics if positive.

Issue 3: Asthma (pre-existing, stable)
- Uses a preventative inhaler morning and night (name/dose not documented); no recent exacerbations.
- No current wheeze, cough, or SOB.
- Continues PRN antihistamine for hay fever.

Medications:
- Preventative asthma inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (taken twice daily).
- Rescue/reliever inhaler held but “not used” – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- OTC antihistamine – name/dose/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma.
- Hay fever.

Social History:
- Lives with wife.
- Non-smoker.
- Occasional alcohol use.
- Works for a health technology company; currently less productive due to fatigue.
- Usually active walker; exercise reduced.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals or in-consult physical findings documented (remote consultation; photo of rash reviewed).

Plan:
- Arrange blood tests: CBC, renal profile, liver function, thyroid profile, inflammatory markers, Lyme serology (per doctor).
- Patient to book phlebotomy via support line.
- Telephone follow-up approximately one week after blood draw to review results.
- If Lyme serology positive: commence appropriate antibiotic regimen.
- Reassess fatigue/myalgia based on results; consider further work-up if labs unrevealing.
- Continue current asthma and antihistamine medications; encourage regular inhaler use.
- Return earlier if new symptoms develop (fever, joint swelling, neurological deficits, worsening fatigue).

● Missing/expected elements:
  – Drug allergies not elicited.
  – Complete medication reconciliation (names, doses) not obtained.
  – No vitals, physical exam findings.
  – No detailed systemic review of mood/sleep, though mood briefly addressed.
● Internal conflicts: None noted.
● Transcript quality: Clear; occasional cut-offs/inaudible words but overall understandable.
